summary.text: A 4-year-old girl came to the hospital because a grade 3/6 continuous murmur was heard at the left side of the chest; she had no obvious symptoms. Transthoracic echocardiography showed a significantly enlarged right coronary artery of 9.0 mm opening at the right atrium, with mild pulmonary stenosis and a big atrial septal defect, and angiography confirmed the diagnosis.

article_limitations: Table 1 and the series statistics describe 32 institutional records from May 2001 to January 2015; the source never states which rows (if any) correspond to Cases 1-5, and attribute matching is not literal, so table rows are not assigned to patients and no measurement series is built for them.
Percentages and counts of the 32-record review (murmur, symptoms, drainage sites, treatment) are cohort statements and are not copied to individual cases.
The Case 3 paragraph cites Fig. 2 panels that belong to the Case 2 figure; Fig. 3 is attributed to Case 3 by its caption content.
Operation types, dates and exact ages at follow-up are not stated for the five cases; no values were inferred.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the five images are inspected in visual.json.
The article declares no supplementary material.
